messages:
maria: Heads-up — bringing up a new quantized model (gulliver-qa-lite, PTQ 4-bit) in a small canary. Seeing intermittent drops of the "actions" array when we use streaming tool-calls. Attaching a raw stream sample below.

kevin: Huh, that sounds like a chunk boundary/tokenization issue. Seen something similar on a different model.

sasha: Can you paste the raw stream fragments you captured?

maria: Sure — here's a minimal reproduction of the raw chunks we got (order preserved):

```
{"type":"chunk","text":"{\"id\":1,\"result\":{\"message\":\"ok\",\"actions\":[{\"name\":\"open\",\"args\":{"}
```

```
{"type":"chunk","text":"\"file\":\"/tmp/file.txt\"}}]}}\n"}
```

maria: When reassembled our parser sometimes ends up missing the actions array (it returns null) or fails to parse. The model output looks split across tokens that change between fp16 and 4-bit.

kevin: Is the frequency different between quant and fp16?

maria: Yes — fp16 ~1/50 failures, 4-bit PTQ ~4/50 in the same workload. So quantization exacerbates it.

tara: Could be streaming chunks being cut at tokenization boundaries that the quantized model prefers. Also check KV-cache shard boundaries if you're using sharded runtime.

sasha: Quick experiment: try disabling chunked_streaming in the canary runtime and run the same sample.

maria: Did that this morning. Failure rate dropped from ~8% to ~2% (small sample). Will run a larger sweep.

infra-bot: deploy 6319998888 -> canary/gulliver-liteq: feature toggle `chunked_streaming=false` applied at 13:52 UTC — monitoring.

maria: Another mitigation we tried: wrap tool-call output in a sentinel envelope on the model side (e.g., `---BEGIN_JSON---` / `---END_JSON---`) — that reduces parse failures but adds ~30-60ms per call.

kevin: For long-term: make the parser tolerant + add reassembly validation. Two concrete ideas:
- ndjson length-prefix framing at the runtime boundary (so you never rely on chunk boundaries),
- post-reassembly JSON sanity check and automatic retry with non-streaming fallback when parse fails.

sasha: Agreed. Also add a micro-benchmark comparing: fp16 vs 4-bit PTQ vs hybrid-quant on the same prompts (N=1000) to measure both parse-failure rate and latency/cost tradeoffs.

maria: Plan I'm running today:
1) ndjson-wrap patch on the client side + 500-sample run (int4 + fp16)
2) larger 5k run with `chunked_streaming=false` and with sentinel wrapper
3) collect parse-fail rate, retry counts, and added latency per-call

tara: Ping @kevin for the ndjson spec + test harness.

kevin: I'll draft a tiny spec (length-prefix + simple CRC) and a harness script that simulates chunk boundaries. Will post by EOD.

maria: Thanks — I'll post results in this thread once the 5k run finishes. :thumbsup:
